title: balance.json `warnings` lead-time fields (node_strained/critical, pipe_pressure) are parsed + validated + folded into catalog_hash but never consumed anywhere — the claimed 'UI reads the leads' telegraph does not exist
evidence:
core/catalog.odin:197-199:
	node_strained_lead_ticks:   u64, // 🟡 lead time to failure (GDD: 30 s)
	node_critical_lead_ticks:   u64, // 🔴 lead time (GDD: 10 s)
	pipe_pressure_lead_ticks:   u64, // pressure lead time (GDD: 20 s)
core/catalog.odin:532-534:
			b.warnings.node_strained_lead_ticks = u64(jint(wobj, "node_strained_lead_ticks", 0))
			b.warnings.node_critical_lead_ticks = u64(jint(wobj, "node_critical_lead_ticks", 0))
			b.warnings.pipe_pressure_lead_ticks = u64(jint(wobj, "pipe_pressure_lead_ticks", 0))
core/catalog.odin:541-542:
		if b.warnings.node_strained_lead_ticks == 0 || b.warnings.node_critical_lead_ticks == 0 ||
			b.warnings.pipe_pressure_lead_ticks == 0 {
app/render/view.odin:338-342:
	step: u32 = 16 // slow amber pulse ~1.25 Hz @ 20 Hz logic
	glyph := "!"
	if lvl == .Red {
		col = p.state_critical
		step = 8 // fast critical pulse ~2.5 Hz
core/warnings.odin:42-44:
// (ODN-1). The lead times (strained 30 s / critical 10 s / pressure 20 s —
// GDD Numerical Design) live in balance.json `warnings`; the UI reads them
// from there (they are not re-stated here).
(grep across core/app/harness finds NO reader of these three fields beyond the parse + `== 0` validation above; the only real lead in the system is demand.json's set-piece forecast_lead_ticks.)
detail: The GDD M5 node/pipe lead times are data with no mechanism: the telegraph fires the tick strain crosses a threshold, no countdown/lead surface exists, while the in-code claims ('The UI reads the leads from here for the telegraph') are false and the fields force the all-goldens catalog_hash re-bless.
recommended_fix: Consume the leads (e.g. drive the ring pulse step or a node/pipe 'to-critical' countdown from them), or drop the three fields from Warning_Balance + balance.json and re-bless once.

title: Ring pulse is 16x slower than documented: envelope cycle = 16 × step ticks → 12.8 s amber / 6.4 s red (0.078/0.156 Hz), not the '~1.25 Hz / ~2.5 Hz' the comments and art-direction §6.1 specify
evidence:
app/render/view.odin:204:
PULSE16 :: [16]f32{0.04, 0.18, 0.38, 0.55, 0.71, 0.84, 0.93, 0.99, 1.0, 0.96, 0.86, 0.71, 0.53, 0.35, 0.18, 0.05}
app/render/view.odin:210-213:
pulse_factor :: proc(tick: u64, node_id: u32, step: u32) -> f32 {
	table := PULSE16 // local copy — a constant can't be indexed by a runtime index
	idx := (tick + u64(node_id) * 5) / u64(step) & 15
	return table[idx]
}
app/render/view.odin:338,342:
	step: u32 = 16 // slow amber pulse ~1.25 Hz @ 20 Hz logic
	step = 8 // fast critical pulse ~2.5 Hz
(detail: idx advances 1 per `step` ticks; a full 16-step envelope = 16×step ticks = 256 amber / 128 red ticks @ 20 Hz = 12.8 s / 6.4 s per swell — the comment values are the table-step rate 20/16 and 20/8, not the pulse-cycle Hz.)
detail: Art-direction §6.1/epic-4-context pins 'ring pulse rate ~1.2 Hz strained, fast ~2.5 Hz critical'; the rendered swell is 16× slower and the code comments mis-state the rate. Escalation language (2×) survives; cosmetic, deterministic, never feeds state.
recommended_fix: Either use step ≈ 1 (amber) and make red visibly faster (e.g. 2-step table stride via a second table), or correct the comments to state the true cycle rate.

title: Warnings fail-fast rows are bypassable: amber=0 passes '0 <= amber < red <= 100' yet strain_level is inclusive so zero-strain nodes read Amber (E24 neutrality broken under legal data); a negative lead wraps through u64(jint(...)) and passes the '> 0' rejection
detail: ODN-5 fail-fast is the only defense for data-driven thresholds; the shipped 70/90/600/200/400 values are fine, but a legal-but-degenerate ladder (amber 0) or negative lead passes load and breaks the no-warning-on-healthy contract.
recommended_fix: Require amber >= 1 in the ladder check and parse leads via jint_strict into i64 with a `lead < 0` rejection before the u64 cast (mirror the demand.json forecast_lead_ticks row).

title: Forecast panel hardcodes 'SURGE' for every set-piece row instead of reading an archetype name from the catalog — any future non-surge set-piece is mislabeled
evidence:
app/render/forecast.odin:22:
// set-piece inside its forecast window: "<CLASS> SURGE ×N — 12s" (or "NOW"
app/render/forecast.odin:52:
		mult := fmt.aprintf("SURGE x%d", f.multiplier, allocator = context.temp_allocator)
(Forecast_Entry carries sp_index/class/multiplier/start_tick/countdown/active — no archetype name field; the era-3 set-piece is the only one today, so the label is currently accurate.)
detail: The weather report is a data-driven read (ODN-5) but invents its archetype label in code; 4.2's crisis archetypes will add set-pieces and the panel would name them all 'SURGE'.
recommended_fix: Carry the set-piece's id/display name into Forecast_Entry (serialized) or resolve it from the demand catalog via sp_index, and drop the hardcoded string.
